skill.name: claude-code-guide
skill.description: A Chinese-language guide for learning Claude Code workflows, tools, MCP setup, hooks, and advanced development patterns.
skill.summary: Learn Claude Code features, workflows, MCP integration, hooks, and practical development patterns from a structured guide.
skill.author: 2025Emma

security_audit.summary: The skill is a documentation-heavy Claude Code guide, and many static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, template literals, examples, and resource links. Real risks remain in copyable automation examples that print secrets, use sudo, grant access to hidden Claude directories, mine Claude logs and state, and demonstrate autonomous shell workflows without strong safety boundaries.

remediation.issue: Secret handling examples print or reference sensitive values.
remediation.suggestion: Replace commands like echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY with safe verification steps that check whether a variable is set without displaying its value.

remediation.issue: Automation examples access ~/.claude logs, state, temp files, and performance databases.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit privacy warnings, redaction steps, and least-privilege paths. Avoid recommending /add-dir ~/.claude or mining raw Claude logs.

remediation.issue: Shell examples include privileged or persistent automation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove sudo from automated recovery flows, add confirmation gates, and mark long-running background loops as conceptual rather than copy-paste-ready.

remediation.issue: The sqlite3 agent selector example interpolates shell variables into SQL.
remediation.suggestion: Show parameterized queries or strict allowlists for task_type and complexity before querying local telemetry.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Claude State and Log Mining Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The guide describes hooks and commands that mine ~/.claude logs and state, then feed extracted patterns into memory or context. This can expose private prompts, project paths, errors, and workflow history if copied without redaction.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple examples explicitly read ~/.claude logs or state and use the results to update memory or context. This is a clear privacy risk even though the content is instructional.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Autonomous Shell Automation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The guide presents a continuous shell loop that starts monitors, research scripts, meta-learning scripts, and autonomous agent spawning. If copied, it can create persistent background activity and broad local command execution without clear consent boundaries.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code is presented as an example rather than active payload, but it explicitly starts long-running automation and deploys generated agents. The risk is high if users paste it into hooks or workflows.

semantic_findings.title: SQL Injection Risk in Agent Selector Example
semantic_findings.description: The smart-agent-selector example interpolates TASK_TYPE and COMPLEXITY directly into a sqlite3 query. A crafted task type or complexity value could alter the query when users adapt the script.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The SQL query directly embeds shell variables inside quoted SQL. The example is instructional, but the injection pattern is concrete and copyable.

content.value_statement: Claude Code users need a clear path from basic commands to advanced workflows. This guide organizes tools, MCP setup, hooks, task management, and practical examples in one learning resource.
actual_capabilities: Explains core Claude Code tools, including REPL, artifacts, web search, web fetch, and conversation search.
Shows file analysis workflows for counting, searching, reading, and extracting content from large files.
Documents MCP configuration concepts, server types, authentication methods, and tool usage patterns.
Describes hook setup ideas for formatting, testing, logging, notifications, and command automation.
Provides examples for data analysis, file search, network fetching, testing, code review, and troubleshooting.
limitations: Most material is instructional documentation, not an executable automation package.
The guide is primarily written in Chinese and may require translation for other teams.
Some examples are conceptual and need safety review before being copied into real hooks or scripts.
Claude Code behavior changes over time, so users should verify details against current official documentation.

use_cases.title: Onboard new Claude Code users
use_cases.description: Use the guide to teach commands, tool permissions, file workflows, and safe development habits.

use_cases.title: Plan advanced development workflows
use_cases.description: Review the workflow patterns for testing, code review, task tracking, and iterative implementation.

use_cases.title: Evaluate MCP and hook ideas
use_cases.description: Study the MCP and hook sections before designing integrations with external systems or local automation.

prompt_templates.title: Learn the basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Claude Code guide to explain the core tools I should learn first. Keep the explanation simple and include safe next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a file analysis workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this guide, create a step-by-step workflow for analyzing a large Markdown or source file with Claude Code.

prompt_templates.title: Review an MCP setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the MCP guidance to review my planned server configuration. Point out missing safety checks, secret handling issues, and setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design safe automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hook and workflow sections to propose a safe Claude Code automation plan. Include permission boundaries, confirmation steps, and rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: Explain which Claude Code tools I should learn first.
output_examples.output: A prioritized learning path covering REPL, artifacts, file reading, search, web tools, and permission-aware Bash usage.

output_examples.input: Help me create a workflow for analyzing a large README.
output_examples.output: A staged workflow with file size checks, heading extraction, targeted reads, keyword searches, and a final summary process.

output_examples.input: Review my hook automation idea for safety.
output_examples.output: A safety checklist that limits file access, avoids secret exposure, requires confirmations, and separates conceptual examples from production scripts.

best_practices: Treat shell, hook, MCP, and filesystem examples as templates that require local security review before use.
Start with read-only workflows and add write or execution permissions only when the need is clear.
Cross-check version-sensitive Claude Code behavior against current official documentation.
anti_patterns: Do not copy sudo, rm, background loop, or hook examples into production without safeguards.
Do not expose API keys, JWT secrets, Claude logs, or hidden configuration files while following examples.
Do not grant Claude Code access to broad home-directory paths when a narrow project path is enough.

faq.question: Is this skill an executable tool?
faq.answer: No. It is mainly a documentation guide with examples and workflows for Claude Code users.

faq.question: Who should use this guide?
faq.answer: Developers, platform engineers, and technical teams who want to learn Claude Code features and workflow patterns.

faq.question: Does it support Codex as well as Claude?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code support, but the content focuses on Claude Code concepts.

faq.question: Can I copy the shell examples directly?
faq.answer: Review them first. Some examples need confirmation gates, least-privilege paths, and secret redaction before real use.

faq.question: Does the guide cover MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains MCP concepts, configuration locations, server types, authentication methods, and tool usage patterns.

faq.question: What is the main safety concern?
faq.answer: Some advanced examples access hidden Claude files, logs, secrets, or privileged commands. Treat those as conceptual unless secured.
